_readme: Minimal starter config -- this is what `jam init` scaffolds into a new project, and the LOWEST layer of the config stack. Keys starting with '_' are comments; JSON has none of its own. Two roles and one coding agent are enough to run a session; add more as you need them. Your personal setup (extra roles, extra coding agents, models, tokens) belongs in the GLOBAL config at ~/.config/jamsession/, where every project picks it up -- see `jam config layers`.
_layers_note: Merge order, lowest precedence first: this file, then ~/.config/jamsession/jamsession.json, then ~/.config/jamsession/jamsession.local.json, then ./jamsession.json, then ./jamsession.local.json. Later layers win key by key; arrays are replaced whole. Run `jam config layers` to see which of these exist, and `jam config raw` for the merged result.

nudge._note: Nudges are deliberately one short line. The real payload always sits on disk in the inbox, so a garbled or missed nudge never loses a message.
nudge.template: [JAM] {count} new message(s) from {from} -- run: jam read --next

defaults._note: Inherited by every role. Anything here can be overridden per role.

coding_agents._note: How to launch each CLI. 'args' is always emitted. Each 'optional_args' group is emitted only if every placeholder in it resolves non-empty, so an unset model cleanly drops --model instead of passing "". Placeholders: {model} {brief} {brief_text} {instance} {role} {session} {cwd} {workdir} {settings} {color}.

claude._note: Agents run unattended, so permission prompts are fatal: a fleet that stops for approval every few minutes does not work. An --allowedTools allowlist was tried first and is NOT sufficient -- Claude Code refuses to statically match any command containing shell syntax (quotes, $(), pipes) or an env-var prefix, which is most real jam invocations. Hence --dangerously-skip-permissions. Scope the risk with worktree roles and a clean git tree, or set this back to ["--permission-mode","acceptEdits"] and babysit the panes.

no_subagents._note: claude renamed the subagent tool Task -> Agent in v2.1.63; both names are still live strings in the 2.1.220 binary and claude --help documents --disallowedTools as 'Comma or space-separated list', so we pass both to be safe whichever one the installed version honours. There is no env var that fully disables the subagent tool; the closest real one is CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS (v2.1.198+, only the built-in Explore/Plan agents).

_roles_note: A role is a seat at the table, not a person: max_instances controls how many agents can hold it at once. Give a role 'worktree: true' when its agents edit code, so concurrent instances cannot collide in the same tree. Add the rest of your roles (explorer, tester, reviewer, debugger, support) in the global config.

orchestrator.description: Owns the goal. Decomposes work, dispatches it, and integrates the results.

implementor.description: Writes and edits production code. Small, reviewable diffs.
